pattern: cat chewed or licked any part of a lily (Lilium/Hemerocallis) incl. pollen or vase water
red_flags: lily exposure in cat|any lily part or pollen
source: ASPCA APCC; Merck Vet Manual - Lily toxicosis

pattern: male cat repeatedly straining in litter box with little or no urine; may cry or lick genitals
red_flags: male cat straining with no urine|possible urinary blockage
source: Merck Vet Manual - Feline lower urinary tract disease

pattern: cat has not eaten for more than 24 hours; may be hiding; otherwise subtle signs
source: Merck Vet Manual - Hepatic lipidosis in cats

pattern: cat was given or got into acetaminophen (Tylenol/paracetamol)
source: ASPCA APCC; Merck Vet Manual - Acetaminophen toxicosis

pattern: cat breathing with mouth open or panting at rest; fast breathing or belly heaving
source: Merck Vet Manual - Dyspnea in cats

pattern: healthy indoor-only cat; owner asks whether vaccines and checkup are needed
source: AAHA/AAFP Feline Vaccination Guidelines

pattern: adult cat vomited a hairball once; eating drinking and acting normal
source: Merck Vet Manual - Vomiting in cats

pattern: dog flea product (permethrin) applied to a cat; twitching or tremors
source: ASPCA APCC; Merck Vet Manual - Pyrethrin/permethrin toxicosis

pattern: older cat drinking and urinating more and losing weight over weeks
source: Merck Vet Manual - Chronic kidney disease

pattern: dog ate chocolate (esp. dark or baking chocolate)
source: ASPCA APCC; Merck Vet Manual - Chocolate toxicosis

pattern: dog ate sugar-free gum/candy/peanut butter containing xylitol (birch sugar)
source: ASPCA APCC; Merck Vet Manual - Xylitol toxicosis

pattern: dog ate grapes or raisins
source: ASPCA APCC; Merck Vet Manual - Grape and raisin toxicosis

pattern: deep-chested dog with swollen hard belly; retching without bringing anything up; restless
source: Merck Vet Manual - Gastric dilatation-volvulus

pattern: dog after exercise in heat: heavy panting; drooling; wobbly; very red gums
source: Merck Vet Manual - Heatstroke

pattern: adult dog vomited once; now eating drinking and playing normally
source: Merck Vet Manual - Vomiting in dogs

pattern: dog limping on one leg for a day; bears some weight; no swelling or wound; otherwise well
source: Merck Vet Manual - Lameness in dogs

pattern: honking dry cough after boarding or daycare; otherwise bright and eating
source: Merck Vet Manual - Canine infectious respiratory disease

pattern: young puppy with diarrhea; may be incompletely vaccinated
red_flags: diarrhea in young or unvaccinated puppy
source: Merck Vet Manual - Canine parvovirus; AAHA Canine Vaccination Guidelines

pattern: senior dog drinking much more water and urinating more over a few weeks
red_flags: new increased thirst in senior dog
source: Merck Vet Manual - Polyuria and polydipsia

pattern: dog ate ibuprofen/Advil/naproxen tablets
source: ASPCA APCC; Merck Vet Manual - NSAID toxicosis

pattern: dog ate rat or mouse bait
source: ASPCA APCC; Merck Vet Manual - Rodenticide toxicosis

pattern: dog swallowed a sock or toy; now vomiting repeatedly and not keeping food down
source: Merck Vet Manual - Gastrointestinal obstruction

pattern: small long-backed dog yelping when picked up; hunched; wobbly back legs
red_flags: hind limb weakness with back pain
source: Merck Vet Manual - Intervertebral disc disease

pattern: red moist itchy patch that pet keeps licking or scratching
source: Merck Vet Manual - Pyotraumatic dermatitis

pattern: pet shaking head and scratching ear; odor or dark debris
source: Merck Vet Manual - Otitis externa

pattern: mild clear or slightly cloudy eye discharge; eye open; no squinting
source: Merck Vet Manual - Conjunctivitis

pattern: pet having a seizure: paddling; jaw chomping; unresponsive; may lose bladder
source: Merck Vet Manual - Seizure disorders

pattern: pet suddenly collapsed or fainted; weak; may have pale gums
source: Merck Vet Manual - Collapse and weakness

pattern: pet has not drunk water for about a day; quieter than usual
source: Merck Vet Manual - Dehydration

pattern: pet tore a toenail; some bleeding that slows with pressure; limping slightly
source: Merck Vet Manual - Nail disorders

pattern: owner sees fleas or flea dirt; mild scratching; skin otherwise ok
source: Merck Vet Manual - Fleas

pattern: pet ate a significant amount of onion or garlic (e.g. a dish of onions)
red_flags: onion or garlic ingestion in quantity
source: ASPCA APCC; Merck Vet Manual - Allium toxicosis

pattern: pet ate a cannabis edible; wobbly; dribbling urine; dilated pupils
source: ASPCA APCC; Merck Vet Manual - Marijuana toxicosis

pattern: pet licked antifreeze (sweet-tasting puddle in garage)
source: ASPCA APCC; Merck Vet Manual - Ethylene glycol toxicosis

pattern: adult pet with one or two soft stools after a treat; bright; eating normally
source: Merck Vet Manual - Diarrhea

pattern: photo: normal coat and skin; no visible lesions

pattern: photo: red inflamed itchy skin (paws/belly/armpits) with hair loss

pattern: photo: pustules/papules; crusts; circular scaly collarettes; moist infected skin

pattern: photo: greasy darkened thickened skin or patchy scaly hair loss (yeast/fungal)

pattern: photo: normal coat and skin; no visible lesions
